## What the papers show (headline)

Scores sit at **14/20 on both papers** and the pattern is consistent:

1. **Time management is the main leak.** On both 09/16 papers he rushed or blanked the last stretch
   (Q16–20: "ran out of time", one question skipped, several "educated guess"). Roughly 4–6 marks per paper
   are lost to the clock, not to ability. → a **timing drill** (last 5 questions in 15 min) matters more than
   new content.
2. **Paper 2 (reasoning) — he second-guesses.** Many "C or D?", "B?", "E??" — he reaches the right region but
   cannot *confirm*. → drill **verification methods** (test a value, check a boundary), not more theory.
3. **Topic gaps** — the **09/04 audit** sharpened these. Almost every wrong/flagged question sits in one of
   three areas: **coordinate geometry (circles & the plane)**, **differentiation / stationary points**, and
   **range / max–min of rational & trig functions**. Below those: logs, ceiling integrals, and trig in
   unfamiliar form. See the **[09/04 error audit](set_2026-09-04.qmd)** for the question-by-question map.

His weak list overlaps ~90 % with the existing clinics, so lessons should **reuse** them rather than rebuild.

::: {.callout-tip}
## The three sessions to run next (Session 1 = Triangles, done last week ✓)

1. **Coordinate geometry — circles & the plane.** His loudest gap: on 09/04 Paper 1 the two wrong questions
   and both flagged ones were circles/geometry (100 concentric circles, tangent lines, distances, regions).
   → **[Coordinate geometry clinic](../../lessons/coordinate_geometry_clinic/class_material.qmd)**.
2. **Differentiation & stationary points.** Five graded/flagged items across both 09/04 papers, all "find the
   turning points, then reason" (Mock 2 Q1, Q14; Paper 1 tangents; 09/16 P2 Q18).
   → **[Differentiation clinic](../../lessons/differentiation_clinic/class_material.qmd)** §2 + §4, plus the
   **[min/max of polynomials supplement](../../lessons/differentiation_clinic/supplementary_minmax.qmd)**
   (where a quartic actually turns, and classifying a stationary point that is *not* a turning point — the
   idea behind his Mock 2 Q14).
3. **Range & max–min + confirm-don't-guess.** The $y$-as-parameter method (Mock 2 Q13 rational-in-$\cos x$, Q9
   discriminant), run as a **verify-before-committing** drill, closed with a **timed last-5-in-15-min** block.
   → **[Range clinic](../../lessons/range_clinic/class_material.qmd)**.
:::
